{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox Hurling All-Ireland |year=2009 |image= |dates= 30 May – 6 September 2009 |teams = 12 |team1= Kilkenny |titles= 32nd |captain1= [[Michael Fennelly (hurler)|Michael Fennelly]] |manager1= [[Brian Cody]] |team2= Tipperary |captain2= [[Willie Ryan (Tipperary hurler)|Willie Ryan]] |manager2= [[Liam Sheedy]] |munster= Tipperary |leinster= Kilkenny |ulster= Antrim |connacht= |matches= |totalgoals= |totalpoints= |topscorer= [[File:Colours of Galway.svg|20px|Border]] [[Joe Canning]] (3–46) |poty= [[File:Colours of Kilkenny.svg|20px|Border]] [[Tommy Walsh (hurler, born 1983)|Tommy Walsh]] |previous=[[2008 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2008]] |next = [[2010 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2010]] }} The '''2009 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 123rd staging of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]'s premier [[inter county|inter-county]] [[hurling]] tournament. The draw for the 2000 fixtures took place on 8 October 2008. The championship began on 30 May 2009 and ended on 6 September 2009. [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] were the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 2008|defending champions]]. [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]] and [[Galway GAA|Galway]] joined the [[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship|Leinster Championship]] for the first time. On 6 September 2009, Kilkenny won the championship following a 2–22 to 0–23 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the All-Ireland final. This was their 32nd All-Ireland title overall, their 7th championship of the decade and a record-equalling fourth All-Ireland title in-a-row. Galway's [[Joe Canning]] was the championship's top scorer with 3–46. Kilkenny's [[Tommy Walsh (hurler, born 1983)|Tommy Walsh]] won Hurler of the Year. ==Provincial changes== Due to a lack of competition in their own respective provinces, [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]] and [[Galway GAA|Galway]] pushed for entry to the [[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship|Leinster Championship]]. At a special meeting of [[GAA Congress|Congress]] on 4 October 2008, delegates voted to include Galway and Antrim in a restructured Leinster Championship on a trial basis for three years. [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]], [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] and [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] spoke against the move, however, when put to a vote approximately 80% of delegates voted in favour.{{cite Firstly, [[Galway GAA|Galway]] have had no opposition in the [[Connacht Senior Hurling Championship]] since 2004. Due to this it was decided at a special meeting of the GAA's congress for Galway to join the [[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship]] for a three-year trial period, starting with the 2009 championship. [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]], being the only Tier 1 team in the [[Ulster Senior Hurling Championship]], also participated in the Leinster Championship on a three-year trial period. Antrim also competed in the Ulster Championship which was run as a [[2009 Ulster Senior Hurling Championship|separate tournament]] to the All-Ireland Hurling Championship. 12 [[Counties of Ireland|counties]] participated in Tier 1 of the 2009 Championship. These teams were as follows: * [[Leinster GAA|Leinster]]: [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]], [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]], [[Galway GAA|Galway]], [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]], [[Laois GAA|Laois]], [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] and [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] * [[Munster GAA|Munster]]: [[Clare GAA|Clare]], [[Cork GAA|Cork]], [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]], [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]], [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] '''Provincial Championships''' The Munster championship was played as usual with five teams. The Leinster championship also proceeded as usual, except for the addition of both Antrim and Galway, bringing the total number of competing teams to seven. The Leinster and Munster champions advanced directly to the All-Ireland semi-finals. '''All-Ireland Qualifiers''' The qualifiers gave teams defeated in the provincial championships another chance at winning the All-Ireland. ''Phase 1:'' (2 matches) the three Leinster quarter-finalists and the Munster quarter-finalist play off. ''Phase 2:'' (2 matches) the two Leinster semi-finalists and two Munster semi-finalists play off. ''Phase 3:'' (2 matches) The four winners of Phase 1 and Phase 2 games meet in Phase 3. The two Phase 3 winners advance to the All-Ireland quarter-finals. '''All-Ireland Series''' ''Quarter-finals:'' (2 matches) The defeated Munster and Leinster finalists played the winners of the Phase 3 qualifiers. ''Semi-finals:'' (2 matches) The Munster and Leinster champions played the winners of the quarter-finals. '''Promotion/Relegation''' Promotion and relegation between Tier 1 and Tier 2 was in operation in the 2009 championship. The defeated team in the Round 2 match of the Relegation playoffs was demoted to the [[2010 Christy Ring Cup]], to be replaced by the winners of the [[2009 Christy Ring Cup]]. ==Leinster Senior Hurling Championship == {{main|Leinster Senior Hurling Championship}} {{8TeamBracket-Compact-NoSeeds-Byes | RD1= Quarter-finals | RD2= Semi-finals | RD3= Leinster final | team-width= 100 | score-width= 35 | RD1-team1= '''[[Dublin GAA|Dublin]]''' | RD1-score1= '''2–16''' | RD1-team2= [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]] | RD1-score2= 0–12 | RD1-team3= '''[[Wexford GAA|Wexford]]''' | RD1-score3= '''2–17''' | RD1-team4= [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] | RD1-score4= 0–16 | RD1-team5= [[Laois GAA|Laois]] | RD1-score5= 0–17 | RD1-team6= '''[[Galway GAA|Galway]]''' | RD1-score6= '''5–29''' | RD1-team7= | RD1-score7= | RD1-team8= | RD1-score8= | RD2-team1= '''[[Dublin GAA|Dublin]]''' | RD2-score1= '''0–18''' | RD2-team2= [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] | RD2-score2= 1–13 | RD2-team3= [[Galway GAA|Galway]] | RD2-score3= 3–13 | RD2-team4= '''[[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]]''' | RD2-score4= '''2–20''' | RD3-team1= [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] | RD3-score1= 0–18 | RD3-team2= '''[[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]]''' | RD3-score2= '''2–18''' }} === Quarter-finals === {{football box | date = May 30
